messages.subject: Unstable precisions
parts:
Hi,
Many thanks for answering the question I posted earlier in the week.

I have a model where I am using grouping variables such as whether the area is in an rural or urban area as random effects.
However, when I use more than one of such variables as my iid random effect, at least one of the variables will have a very large precision mean, and it is not always the same variable that has the large precision when I use different combinations of random effect variables. All of my random effect variables are of the same nature, ie. iid for all observations within each level of the category.

I experienced the same problem, with and without using bym.

Having read around, I assumed this is due to prior sensitivity and tried to use the below code,  but I get an error message stating 'Name `correct' in control-argument `control.inla', is void.'


r = inla(..., control.inla = list(
correct = TRUE,
correct.factor = <VALUE>))

Could you help me to solve this problem of large precision please? Is this really caused by prior sensitivity? 

Many thanks
